scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Independent friendship-email reading assessment with original questions, pending pedagogical validation

questions.q: What does Elias imply by calling his account of being busy 'conveniently incomplete'?
choices: His work schedule is less demanding than it appears.
His explanation hides his willingness to send public updates instead of honest letters.
His travels never actually occurred.
His friend has asked for too many explanations.
questions.explanation: Elias recognises that he had time for polished updates but avoided difficult honesty.

questions.q: What is the central difference Elias sees between information and a person?
choices: Personal details cannot be sent over the internet.
Photographs are always less accurate than letters.
Busy travellers have no real friends.
Being easy to locate online is not the same as being emotionally available.
questions.explanation: The ferry-terminal reflection distinguishes sharing location from being able to discuss feeling lost.

questions.q: Why does the former dockworker's account resist the editor's preferred ending?
choices: It denies that anyone helped their neighbours.
It describes only events outside the museum's subject.
It preserves solidarity and resentment together instead of a comforting moral.
It refuses to mention the history of the dock.
questions.explanation: The dockworker describes mutual support coexisting with resentment, challenging a warm simple conclusion.

questions.q: What is the significance of Elias's remark about 'the pleasure of being useful'?
choices: Responding with tidy advice can prevent genuine listening to complexity.
The archive should avoid recording any difficult experiences.
Friends have a duty to solve each other's problems quickly.
The editor should always choose a positive story.
questions.explanation: Elias learns that attention may require relinquishing easy solutions.

questions.q: Why are the father's brief postcards emotionally valuable but insufficient?
choices: They provide detailed accounts of every voyage.
They reveal that he lived in the same town throughout.
They prove the family's difficulties have been overcome.
They mark occasions of thought without compensating for long absences.
questions.explanation: The daughter values the small signals while refusing to romanticise her father's absence.

questions.q: How does Elias contrast the postcards with his own public messages?
choices: The postcards had a more sophisticated style.
Their limited claims were more honest than his polished appearance of completeness.
They contained more factual information.
They were written more frequently than his updates.
questions.explanation: The cards never pretended to convey more than a small greeting.

questions.q: What makes Elias's invitation ethically delicate?
choices: The museum might not have enough seats.
The listening room is intended only for residents.
Its timing might make his renewed interest appear self-serving.
Amara has asked never to receive another invitation.
questions.explanation: He recognises that contacting Amara just before his event could look instrumental.

questions.q: Why would asking Amara to reassure him of his sincerity be unfair?
choices: It would shift the emotional burden of his guilt onto her.
It would remove her opportunity to buy a ticket.
It would require them to revisit every earlier argument.
It would contradict the museum's opening schedule.
questions.explanation: Elias refuses to make Amara responsible for proving that he is a decent friend.

questions.q: What makes declining the invitation a genuinely acceptable possibility?
choices: Elias expects her to send a substitute attendee.
He will send further messages until she accepts.
He treats a refusal as evidence against the friendship.
He explicitly removes any duty to attend or give an excuse.
questions.explanation: He says she may decline without justification and that her presence is not owed.

questions.q: What does Elias hope modest correspondence might allow?
choices: A precise restoration of their earlier relationship.
Two changed people to connect without recreating a reassuring memory.
An immediate return to daily replies.
A formal way to test whether Amara still cares.
questions.explanation: He values correspondence that allows both friends to have changed.
